question.text: A moving coil galvanometer has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> turns and each turn has an area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The magnetic field produced by the magnet is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> and the deflection in the coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>05</mn></math> radian when a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi></math> is passed through it. The torsional constant of the suspension wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>rad</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______ .

solution.text:
Torque produced in a moving coil galvanometer is, τ=BINAsinϕ.

Let torsional constant of the suspension wire be C, then Cθ=BINAsin90°

⇒C= BINA θ=0.01×10×10-3×100×2×10-40.05

=4×10-5 N-m/rad.

Therefore, x=4.
